transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-02 15:00 UTC
Duration: 38 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Arjun Patel (Redwood SE), Caitlin Jones (Acme - Head of Product), Omar Khan (Acme - ML Eng), Raj Singh (Acme - Infra)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for taking the time today. I'm Maya, I'm the AE on the account, and with me is Arjun from our SE team. Quick intro, purpose of the call is to walk through Redwood's PLG quickstart and understand Acme's goals for a quick POC.

[00:18] Caitlin Jones: Thanks Maya. We're trying to spin up a prototype assistant in our support product. Main asks are: how fast can we get to first token, what costs look like, and any security blockers for going with hosted vs dedicated.

[00:30] Arjun Patel: Great. Typical. Quick note - the quickstart is intentionally minimal: sign up, get free credits, API keys, and you can hit text-gen and embeddings in under 15 minutes. Time-to-first-token usually depends on auth and firewall rules but for most customers it's literally a few minutes.

[01:02] Omar Khan: When you say free credits, is that account-level credits or project-level? Also we have strict data retention policies - can you confirm we can disable retention on hosted?

[01:18] Maya Chen: Account-level credits we grant for quickstarts, and we've got guidance docs. For hosted the default is transient logs for debugging but we have controls and can turn off retention for enterprise, and there's Dedicated/Private options for full isolation. We'll share the exact policy doc.

[01:45] Raj Singh: From infra side, our security folks will ask for SOC 2, audit logs, SSO, and VPC peering options. If we go hosted, can we do SAML SSO and restrict egress?

[02:05] Arjun Patel: Yes, SAML SSO and RBAC are supported. For network restrictions, hosted has IP allowlists and regional controls. For stricter requirements we recommend Redwood Dedicated or Private where you get customer VPC, inbound peering, and you manage keys via KMS/HSM integrations.

[02:35] Caitlin Jones: Great. For the POC, we're starting with 10k monthly tokens estimate, then potentially 1-2M if it goes to production. We also care about latency - sub 300ms for typical generation is ideal.

[02:50] Arjun Patel: OK that's helpful. For 10k tokens the hosted API is usually the easiest and most cost-effective. Latency depends on model choice and sequence length; we can recommend small LLMs or quantized variants for low latency. We also have Redwood Dedicated if you need more predictable throughput.

[03:15] Omar Khan: Can you give an example of time-to-first-token if we use a small open model vs a larger base model?

[03:28] Arjun Patel: For a small 7B open model, cold-start time is negligible with our runtime optimizations - typically first token in ~100-200ms for short prompts on hosted in the same region. Larger 13/70B models might have slightly higher overhead, 200-400ms first token depending on KV cache warm state. Those are ballpark. We'll share a benchmark sheet.

[04:01] Maya Chen: Quick qualification - who will own the POC internally and what's your timeline?

[04:08] Caitlin Jones: Omar will lead the integration, and Raj will validate infra/security. Timeline: want a working prototype in 2-3 weeks, decision by end of quarter.

[04:22] Maya Chen: Great - that aligns with our quickstart path. We'll provide credits and a step-by-step quickstart repo that gets you to first token.

[04:35] Raj Singh: One more infra question - if we hit constraints or need lower latency, what's the migration path from hosted to Dedicated? Is it seamless?

[04:50] Arjun Patel: We've designed it to be as seamless as possible. Same API surface, model naming and rollout policies. You can pin model versions and flip routing to dedicated pools. There are ops steps for networking and capacity mapping, but it's not a rewrite.

[05:08] Caitlin Jones: About data residency - some of our data is EU only. Can hosted guarantee routing to EU region?

[05:20] Maya Chen: Yes, you can pick region endpoints and we can restrict a workspace to EU only. For stricter residency we recommend Dedicated or Private so data never leaves your VPC.

[05:33] Omar Khan: For evals, do you provide tools for tracking quality regressions? We run A/B evaluations and want alerts if model quality drops after a rollout.

[05:44] Arjun Patel: Redwood Optimize includes quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to prompt sets and evals. For quickstart we can show a minimal setup and how to hook your evals.

[06:00] Maya Chen: Let's walk through a quick onboarding flow - I'll describe steps and Arjun will chime in with tech details. Step 1: sign up and create workspace. Step 2: link SSO if you want. Step 3: generate API key. Step 4: run sample curl or SDK to call text-gen. Step 5: validate outputs and iteratively tune.

[06:27] Arjun Patel: On the SDK side, we have Node/Python examples. For embeddings, we include batching best practices. Also, our runtime supports KV/prefix caching to speed up repeated prefixes which helps cost and latency.

[06:42] Omar Khan: Any quotas on free credits? We have multiple engineers who might try the quickstart.

[06:49] Maya Chen: The quickstart credit is single account but we can extend or create a trial org for your team. We'll make sure engineers can self-serve within the trial org.

[07:00] Caitlin Jones: For the POC we'll likely start with the hosted quickstart and demo to execs. If infra likes it, we may want a Dedicated pilot.

[07:12] Raj Singh: For Dedicated pilot, what are the lead times and cost estimate?

[07:18] Arjun Patel: Typical Dedicated pilots are a few weeks to provision (depending on GPU availability) and we offer short-term reserved capacity for pilot. Cost depends on selected model and instance types. We'll send a sample pricing/packaging sheet.

[07:36] Maya Chen: Sounds like a plan. Omar - for the integration, do you have a preferred sample prompt set or dataset you can share? Even a small sample helps us run internal latency/cost estimates.

[07:46] Omar Khan: I can pull a subset of our support transcripts - remove PII and share a 200 prompt sample.

[07:52] Arjun Patel: Perfect. We'll run the quick benchmark on our side against the small model and return with token-level cost and median latency.

[08:05] Caitlin Jones: One thing - we need SOC2 Type II and a vendor security questionnaire filled. Is that standard?

[08:15] Maya Chen: Yes, we have a security packet that includes SOC2 attestation, ISO docs, our data handling policy, and a completed vendor questionnaire template. I'll attach that to the follow-up email.

[08:30] Raj Singh: Also curious about encryption keys - do you support customer-managed keys (CMK) for Dedicated or Private?

[08:38] Arjun Patel: Yes CMK via KMS/HSM is supported for Dedicated/Private. Hosted supports encryption at rest and in transit with provider-managed keys.

[08:48] Caitlin Jones: Ok good. Can you also confirm retention windows and the ability to opt-out of model training/data ingestion?

[08:58] Maya Chen: Hosted does not use customer content to train models by default, and you can opt out. We'll include the policy link. Dedicated/Private gives you full control - nothing leaves your environment unless you enable it.

[09:12] Omar Khan: Walk me through an example curl to get started - I want to hand it to my engineers now if possible.

[09:18] Arjun Patel: Sure, here's a quick example we usually share: curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>' -d '{"input":"Summarize this support ticket..."}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate. We'll include the exact sample in the quickstart repo; also SDK snippets for Python/Node.

[09:40] Caitlin Jones: If we start the trial today, can we expect to have a demo to execs in two weeks?

[09:47] Maya Chen: Yes that's realistic. We'll prioritize the onboarding and Arjun can support with tuning. If we need a demo-ready UX we can help with a slide deck/sample demo.

[10:00] Raj Singh: About cost - can you show token-level unit economics? We need to model monthly spend.

[10:08] Arjun Patel: Absolutely. We'll share a spreadsheet with token cost estimates per model variant plus sample autoscaling/batching knobs that impact unit cost. For the quickstart estimate we'll use the small 7B model for conservative numbers.

[10:28] Maya Chen: Great, I'll summarize next steps.

[10:31] Maya Chen: Action items: 1) Maya to send quickstart link, credits instructions, and security packet. 2) Arjun to run a small benchmark with their 200-sample prompt set and share latency/cost numbers. 3) Caitlin to provide prompt sample and confirm timeline for exec demo.

[10:52] Caitlin Jones: That works. One last Q - do you have any known incompatibilities with our stack? We use GCP primarily and some internal proxies.

[11:03] Arjun Patel: We have customers on GCP, AWS, and Azure. For proxies you'll want to allowlist Redwood endpoints or use outbound proxy configs; we can provide networking docs.

[11:18] Omar Khan: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.

[11:22] Maya Chen: Thanks all - we'll follow up with the links and schedule the tech deep dive.

[11:28] Caitlin Jones: Appreciate it.

[11:30] End of meeting.

Notes: transcript contains occasional transcription artifacts; speaker labels may be slightly off in segments. References: quickstart repo link (sent after call), security packet (attached in follow-up).
